hints.content:
$g'(x)>0$ means $g$ is **increasing**.

$g'(x)<0$ means $g$ is **decreasing**.

$g''(x)>0$ means the slope of $g$ is increasing ($g$ is **concave up**).

$g''(x)<0$ means the slope of $g$ is decreasing ($g$ is **concave down**).

| | $g'(x)>0$ | $g'(x)<0$
:- | :- | :-: | :-:
| | $g$ is **increasing** | $g$ is **decreasing**
$g''(x)>0$ | $g$ is **concave up** |  ![A curve moves upward with increasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/fad1dc95cd761b6e7f4c581c7093841fcf16029a) | ![A curve moves downward with decreasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/88e8d1ff71cbe909ea256814c06e1ff2df39bd5e)
$g''(x)<0$ | $g$ is **concave down** | ![A curve moves upward with decreasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/f9425dbee4d4f73f6188a62f88f637018843d7c8) | ![A curve moves downward with increasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/4d64d76d6423a90abf605dfe2b856e7327f92a0c)

We are asked to find an interval where $g'(x)<0$ and $g''(x)>0$, so we need an interval where the graph of $g$ has this general shape:


![A curve moves downward with decreasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/88e8d1ff71cbe909ea256814c06e1ff2df39bd5e)

Visually, this is where $g'(x)<0$ and $g''(x)>0$.

![The graph of function g has a portion of the curve highlighted. The portion starts in quadrant 2, moves downward concave up, and ends at about (negative 1, negative 50).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/6cbcda5ba8cbd0429787e9dbc0a5d41ef8e49cb8)

Now we can check each option:

Interval | Shape | Is $g'(x)<0$ and $g''(x)>0$?
:-: | :-: | :-:
$-4<x<-2$ | ![A curve moves downward with decreasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/1423ac842506af6991b8e635c34a9d36faf33368) | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
$-1<x<1$ | ![A curve moves upward with increasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/842593fcfd6a52a51cd66950f88ff7cd344d7af3) | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $g''(x)>0$ but $g'(x)>0$.
$3<x<4$ | ![A curve moves downward with increasing steepness.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/08e8b7e5ce7d160e69c506cebdd2552cb4f57715) | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $g'(x)<0$ but $g''(x)<0$.
